sheets.name: README
rows: Traceability view for one regulation-to-SHACL generation run.
Generation is frozen before RDF execution; no ship graph or hidden expected outcome is used here.
events.jsonl is append-only; CSV and Excel sheets are derived views.
Static validation passed and the semantic validator accepted the candidate.
No verified canonical term was available; the generator was not allowed to invent one.
Accepted shapes await the separate bulk evaluator.

sheets.name: ITERATIONS

Deterministic validation prevents acceptance. Semantic validator feedback: Remove or rename the eight invented named shape IRIs in the nltl vocabulary namespace; use SHACL blank-node shapes or a non-canonical shape namespace so deterministic vocabulary validation passes. Also correct the owner mismatch for machineryComponentType: its supplied requiredOwner is ship, but the candidate places it on each machinery component; encode the required ship-owned path without relocating or duplicating the fact. Preserve the existing ship-to-component-to-approvalRecord path, branch alternatives, Category C ice-strengthened applicability, approval policies, evidence status, and operating-ice context.

The ship-owned machineryComponentType is now correctly placed, and the prior namespace issue is resolved. However, the shape does not use machineryComponentType to define or select the applicable propeller blades, propulsion-line, steering-equipment, and appendage components: it applies the approval requirement to every hasComponent value, including unrelated components, while only requiring an unconstrained presence of a ship-level string. Encode the applicability relationship so that approval is checked for each applicable machinery component and not for unrelated components, without relocating or duplicating machineryComponentType. Preserve the existing ship→hasComponent→hasApprovalRecord paths, A/B and ice-strengthened-C alternatives, authority and standard policies, approved status, and Category C operating-ice context.

Repair the applicability encoding. machineryComponentType is correctly ship-owned, but the candidate binds that ship-level value and then applies approval to every hasComponent machineryComponent, so unrelated components are incorrectly mandatory; locate or request a canonical term/path that selects the applicable component set from the ship-owned machineryComponentType without relocating or duplicating that fact. Also eliminate the accidental-pass sh:or structure: an A/B ship can satisfy the C branch because its SPARQL condition is inapplicable, and a non-ice-strengthened Category C ship can satisfy the A/B branch. Encode category applicability so every applicable branch is enforced and only genuinely nonapplicable conditions pass, while preserving the ship→hasComponent→hasApprovalRecord path, required approval status, authority and branch-specific standards, and Category C operating-ice type and concentration evidence.
